name: graph-first-navigation
body:
The ordering discipline the codebase-navigator follows: for any fact about code or structure — declarations, dependencies, containment, enumeration, discovery — the program graph is consulted first, and file tools are confirmatory (open the graph's `path` at its `start_line`/`end_line`) or cover artifacts outside the graph's symbol model. In this model the out-of-graph class denotes an artifact whose symbols the graph lacks: Ruby sources pending `apg-ruby` and binaries lack a frontend, so they appear only as residual `misc` `File` nodes carrying zero Module/Struct/Function facts. Only paths the config scope and the standard exclusions remove lack a node at all.

Both the ordering and the in-graph / out-of-graph artifact-class boundary are baseline: the installed `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` rule 1 states the ordering for ANY code/structure question, discovery and enumeration included, and names both classes; the coherence test `rust.apg.tests.e2e.graph_first_rule_stated_in_navigator_prompt_and_guide` asserts it.

The bundled structural scanner graphs every tracked text/config/packaging file, so tracked `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` (toml), `install.sh` (sh), `.github/workflows/release.yml` (yaml), `apg/config.json` and `opencode-suite/package.json` (json), and `LICENSE` (misc) sit in the graph. The out-of-graph class keeps its symbol-absence meaning: Ruby sources (`Formula/*.rb`, pending `apg-ruby`) and binaries remain residual `misc` `File` nodes carrying zero Module/Struct/Function facts, and only paths the config scope (`apg/config.json`) and the standard exclusions (`.git`, `target`, `node_modules`, `.gitignore`, `--exclude-path`) remove lack a node at all. The sibling note `requirements.note.graph-first-artifact-class-shrink` records the artifact-class boundary.
